title: [PIPELINE TEST — not for publish] Prefix cache reuse cuts serving cost
closing_line: 65% of the tokens in that workload were the same prefix, paid for three times. The fix is a serving-side flag, not a new model.

items.headline: A cache-reuse trick cuts long-context serving cost, and it is a config flag.
items.what_changed: Shared request prefixes get cached once across requests instead of being recomputed for every single one.
items.why_it_matters: Serving cost stops scaling with total tokens and starts scaling with unique tokens.
items.who_should_care: Anyone serving one long system prompt, RAG preamble, or few-shot block to many users.

the_number.label: fewer tokens billed in the example below
notes: Savings scale linearly with how much of the request is repeated prefix.
With n requests sharing a prefix, the ceiling on prefix cost is (n-1)/n of the prefix tokens.
Below roughly 30% shared prefix the effect is not worth the config change.
Not a quality change: outputs are identical, only the accounting differs.

diff.minus: every request recomputes the shared prefix
diff.plus: the prefix is cached once, reused by all requests

items.watch_out: The prefix must be byte-identical -- one changed timestamp invalidates the cache. Cache residency is bounded by memory. A cache shared across tenants is a data-isolation decision, not just a performance one.

example.caption: Nine lines. Runs fully offline, no model download.
example.code:
def approx_tokens(text):
    return max(1, round(len(text) / 4))

prefix = "You are a helpful assistant. " * 40
requests = [prefix + q for q in ("hi", "why is the sky blue?", "can you say that again?")]

naive  = sum(approx_tokens(r) for r in requests)
shared = approx_tokens(prefix) + sum(approx_tokens(r[len(prefix):]) for r in requests)

print(naive, shared, round(1 - shared / naive, 3))
